text: The Abasto Shopping is one of the largest shopping mall centers in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Originally, it functioned as the central wholesale fruit and vegetable market, known as the "Mercado de Abasto," from 1893 to 1984. Since 1999, it has operated as a shopping mall. It is also renowned for being the area where tango singer Carlos Gardel, known as "El Morocho del Abasto" ("the dark-haired guy from Abasto"), lived for most of his life. Today, although located within the Balvanera neighbourhood, the surrounding area is often referred to as Abasto. The shopping center is accessible via the adjacent underground station Carlos Gardel on Line B of the metro (subte). By the end of the 19th century, Buenos Aires was expanding rapidly due to European migration, and following the demolition of the Mercado Modelo near Plaza Lorea, the Devoto brothers, who had acquired land in the Balvanera neighbourhood in 1875, proposed building a supply market. The land was situated near the Sarmiento railway and halfway between La Boca and Olivos, two key zones for fruit and vegetable production. The town hall approved the proposal on November 29, 1888, and the Deliberating Council sanctioned it on January 8, 1889, authorizing the construction of the Mercado Central de Abasto ("Central Supply Market") on a 25,000 m² plot bounded by Corrientes Avenue, Lavalle, Anchorena, and Laprida streets. The municipality permitted the market to sell fruit, vegetables, and other foodstuffs but prohibited meat sales. The former marketeers of Mercado Modelo formed the Sociedad Anónima Mercado de Abasto Proveedor ("Market Supply Provider Anonymous Society") in 1889, which purchased the land and the building rights from the Devoto brothers. Construction began after mayor Francisco Seeber approved the sale, with the first section opening on April 1, 1893, covering 1,300 m². Ten years later, a refrigerated storage facility and an ice factory were established to meet hygiene standards. As population and consumer demand grew, a parking area for horses and vehicles was needed, and in 1928, an annex for retail sales was built between Guardia Vieja, Lavalle, Gallo, and Bustamante streets. Continued demand led to overcrowding, prompting architects José Luis Delpini, Viktor Sulčič, and Raúl Bes to design a new market on the same site. Work began on December 28, 1931, with foundations and was completed in 1934. The new Mercado de Abasto covered 44,000 m² (473,612 sq ft), included railway access, and had underground parking. In 1939, the sale of meat and fish was permitted. On October 14, 1984, the central market was relocated to the present Mercado Central outside Buenos Aires, and the original Abasto market was closed and abandoned. A redevelopment project for a shopping mall was proposed in the mid-1990s. In 1996, the building was sold to "Inversiones y Representaciones Sociedad Anónima" (IRSA), which restored the facade and remodeled the interior. The Abasto Shopping Centre opened in 1999 and currently features many locally known brands such as Akiabara, Cuesta Blanca, and Sarkany, along with a limited number of foreign brands including Adidas, Lacoste, and Nike.
